rows.reason: The P–E loop remanent polarization and the integrated thermal-depolarization charge are independent instrumental measurements of the same poled remanent polarization and should agree at saturation.

The depolarization temperature is independently identified by two different measurement methods—an LCR tan-delta peak and the collapse of remanent polarization from P–E loops—so their values are expected to agree.
The P–E analyzer and shock-discharge current integration are distinct methods estimating the same remanent/released polarization charge density.

The transition temperature inferred from dielectric measurements is compared with that inferred from polarization decay in independently acquired P–E loops, so two instruments/methods assess the same physical transition.
The target Pr(T) was read directly from the temperature-dependent P–E loops, so the relation only reproduces the authors’ derivation.
The target energy density was calculated directly from the remanent polarization using w = Pr^2/(2εε0), so the relation only reproduces the authors' arithmetic.
